transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-06-14
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Zoe (Redwood SE), Lena (Oxbridge CTO), Diego (Platform Eng), Priya (SRE), Sam (Dev Lead)

Summary (auto): Initial discovery to capture p95 targets and concurrency requirements for a streaming summarization product. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency but evaluating Hosted and Private for compliance.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:06] Lena (Oxbridge): lena here, diego, priya, sam on my side.
[00:10] Diego (Oxbridge): yeah hi.
[00:12] Maya: awesome. agenda — align on p95 targets, current infra, tradeoffs hosted/dedicated/private, then propose pilot and next steps. sound good?
[00:20] Sam: yeah, that's perfect.
[00:25] Ethan (Redwood): quick note, i'll surface some numbers from earlier benchmarks and a template for our token/sec scripts.
[00:31] Priya: great. for context — we're building a live doc summarization pipeline, clients stream chunks and expect a near realtime summarized chunk back, then final stitched summary. so streaming latency is critical.
[00:45] Maya: got it. what's your p95 target today?
[00:49] Lena: we want p95 under 300ms for the small chunk replies (like 30-80 tokens responses). for larger stitches maybe 800-1k ms is fine. the bigger ask is sustaining throughput — we expect bursts at peak of about 40 concurrent users producing streams, each at ~2 tokens/sec average, but bursts can go to 8 tokens/sec. overall steady-state ~80k tokens/sec seems like our ballpark — sorry that's a bit rough.
[01:20] Diego: to add, we expect sustained background traffic from other batch jobs, so isolation is important. we'd prefer dedicated pools if costs make sense.
[01:31] Zoe (Redwood): thanks, that helps. couple clarifying q's — when you say 40 concurrent streams is that per region or global?
[01:37] Sam: per region — primarily us-east, but we have EU customers later this year.
[01:42] Ethan: ok. two immediate knobs that affect p95 and throughput: batching (which increases effective tokens/sec but can increase latency if not continuous) and KV/prefix caching (which can eliminate a lot of repeated compute for document-context). are you using prefix caching today?
[01:58] Priya: partially; we have Redis for some context but it's application-level, not model-level KV cache.
[02:05] Ethan: cool, so Redwood's automatic prefix caching can shave p95 a lot for repeated prompts. for streaming we also avoid large batching windows and use continuous batching — keeps tail latency down.
[02:18] Lena: question — for continuous batching, does that mean we might see variability in individual token latency as load fluctuates?
[02:25] Ethan: yes some variability — we tune target batch sizes and latency SLOs. for Dedicated you can reserve capacity and set autoscale thresholds to reduce variance.
[02:34] Maya: plus we have routing policies — can route latency-sensitive traffic to Dedicated pools and lower-cost background traffic to hosted variants automatically.
[02:42] Diego: how do fallbacks work if dedicated pool is saturated? can requests failover to hosted?
[02:48] Zoe: yep, can configure model-variant fallbacks and region fallbacks. you'll see slightly different p95 numbers depending on variant/quantization. we also can set graceful degradation so you get a response instead of an error.
[02:59] Sam: pricing question — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated per token?
[03:03] Maya: rough rule — hosted is lower up-front friction but can be higher unit cost at scale; Dedicated reduces unit cost with a reservation. we'll send a pricing sheet with scenario math.
[03:12] Priya: security / compliance — we need SOC2, KMS integration, and audit logs for every request. private VPC is preferable for some customers.
[03:21] Maya: Redwood Private supports a customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integrations. we also provide audit logs and SSO/SAML. we'll include our security deck.
[03:30] Diego: good. can you also share network egress patterns? we need to model our VPC egress.
[03:34] Zoe: yes we'll include a short doc on network topology and recommended NAT/bastion setup.
[03:39] Ethan: back to performance — can i run through a quick baseline sim? two scenarios: A) Dedicated baseline with reserved 2x A100s (or equivalent) serving a 13B quantized model for most responses; B) Hosted multi-tenant with same model. we measure p95 for short responses and sustained tokens/sec across 40 concurrent streams.
[03:58] Lena: that's helpful. what's your expectation for token/sec per GPU for that model?
[04:03] Ethan: ballpark for a 13B with quantization and optimized kernels, a single GPU might do 15k-30k tokens/sec depending on context length and streaming overhead. with KV cache and streaming optimizations you often get higher effective throughput. so you'd probably need 2-4 GPUs to hit your 80k steady. but we'll run real benchmarks.
[04:22] Diego: any way to reduce GPUs with heavier batching?
[04:25] Ethan: yes, but batching trades latency. if you prioritize p95 <300ms we keep small batch windows which costs more compute. another lever is quantization or smaller model variants for less critical routes.
[04:38] Sam: can you do an A/B between a 7B and 13B model to see p95 delta?
[04:42] Zoe: absolutely — pilot can include both. we'll produce per-route dashboards for token-level latency and cost.
[04:49] Priya: around the SDK — do you support client protocol streaming (websockets) or do we need to proxy?
[04:55] Maya: both. hosted supports streaming via HTTP chunked or websockets; Private gives you same runtime but behind your network.
[05:01] Lena: what's the observability granularity — can we get token-level traces and correlation IDs?
[05:06] Ethan: yes, we provide tracing hooks, token-level timing breakdown, and request-level cost. we emit a correlation id you can join with your logs.
[05:14] Maya: ok quick detour — competitors mentioned? anyone evaluating others?
[05:18] Lena: we looked at OpenAI endpoints for quick PoCs, Lambda for on-prem options, and Run:ai for cluster mgmt.
[05:25] Maya: understood.
[05:27] Ethan: proposed pilot plan: two-week bench. week 1: baseline runs on Dedicated config (2-4 gpus), capture p95 short and long, run steady-state token/sec test at reproduced traffic profile. week 2: compare hosted variant and run failure/fallback scenarios + security validation.
[05:46] Diego: timeline-wise we want to make a platform decision in 3-4 weeks, so short pilot asap please.
[05:52] Maya: we can start pilot next Tue — i'll send kickoff invite.
[05:56] Sam: what do you need from us to kick off?
[06:00] Ethan: sample traffic traces (histogram), average prompt/context lengths, and any eval prompts—diego you mentioned you'll share that?
[06:07] Diego: yes i'll pull our kinesis histogram and a small sample of prompts (anonymized).
[06:12] Maya: perfect. i'll also include a suggested benchmark harness (github link) and a pricing spreadsheet — will include roughCommitted vs payg math.
[06:21] Priya: can you also include SLA language and retention defaults?
[06:24] Maya: yes, we'll attach our SLA and data retention options.
[06:27] Zoe: small note on measurements — for streaming p95 we measure from first byte requested to the first chunk of generated text returned, and full-response p95 for non-streamed endpoints. we'll document exact metrics in the pilot spec.
[06:42] Lena: one more question on model versioning and rollouts — how do you handle canarying with dedicated pools?
[06:49] Ethan: routing policies let you send x% of traffic to a canary model variant on either the same pool or a canary pool. we track regressions against baseline prompts and can auto-fallback if quality drops.
[07:01] Sam: okay good. that's reassuring.
[07:04] Maya: anything else?
[07:06] Priya: i want to highlight network egress and encryption at rest — need to see KMS doc.
[07:10] Maya: yes will include.
[07:12] Diego: can you also give an initial cost estimate if we commit 3 months of Dedicated? just rough numbers to present to finance.
[07:18] Maya: yes, we'll add tiered commit examples in the pricing sheet.
[07:22] Ethan: last technical note — we'll instrument a small synthetic test that simulates TCP-level streaming and measures per-token jitter, tail-percentiles, and error rates. that'll give you a clear readiness number.
[07:36] Lena: sounds good.
[07:38] Maya: recap / next steps: redwood to share pilot config, benchmark harness, security deck, pricing sheet. oxbridge to share traffic histograms and prompt samples. setup pilot kickoff next Tue.
[07:53] Sam: thanks everyone.
[07:55] Diego: thanks.
[07:57] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some model/product names are paraphrased; timestamps are approximate.
